findings: Twelve small face medallions surround the pointed center. Their filled regions alternate visually between reddish portions and pale/buff discs; this is an inventory description, not a calendar or illumination assignment.

At least three coarse red-area states can be distinguished visually: no visible red patch (e.g. M02), a narrow red minority patch (M11), and a broad red patch approaching half (M01/M07). Zero refers specifically to visible red area inside the outlined disc, not to absence of every pigment.

The visible boundary of the filled red portion is sufficient for these coarse distinctions, but there is no measured set of fractions, equal-area calibration or cyclic law. Several other red medallions remain unranked.
Nearby writing is abundant, but no inscription has an independently unambiguous explicit attachment in this view. I do not infer repeated textual identity without reading or binding the inscriptions.
uncertainties: Small medallions, uneven pigment and face outlines prevent precise area ratios. The coarse classes are native qualitative judgments, not pixel-segmented measurements.

No-red cases have a visible disc boundary but no internal red/pale boundary; their zero red area is the counted third state. If a later test requires three positive-area red states, this observation does not supply them.
No conclusion about what the red/pale distinction represents, whether it is proportional, or whether the drawing is an instrument.
Negative attachment judgement means no unambiguous connection established by this view, not proof that the text has no semantic relationship.
